facts.statement: Chaoyangsaurus was a member of the Ceratopsia, a group of dinosaurs known as "horned faces".
facts.quote: Chaoyangsaurus belonged to the Ceratopsia (Greek for "horned faces").

facts.statement: Chaoyangsaurus was primarily a herbivore, feeding on plants.
facts.quote: Chaoyangsaurus, like all ceratopsians, was primarily a herbivore.

facts.statement: The remains of Chaoyangsaurus were discovered in 1976 by Cheng Zhengwu at Ershijiazi in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: In 1976, the remains of Chaoyangsaurus were found by Cheng Zhengwu at Ershijiazi, in the Chaoyang area of Liaoning Province in northeastern China.

facts.statement: Chaoyangsaurus did not receive an official scientific name until 1999.
facts.quote: It was not until 1999 that the dinosaur finally received an official name.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Chaoyangsaurus comes from the Tuchengzi Formation, dated to the late Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, IGCAGS V371, has been found in a layer of the Tuchengzi Formation that was in 1999 dated to the late Tithonian.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil consists of a partial skeleton including the lower skull, braincase, lower jaws, seven neck vertebrae, a right shoulder blade, and a right humerus.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton with skull. It contains the lower part and braincase of the skull, the lower jaws, seven neck vertebrae, the right shoulder blade and the right humerus.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Chaoyangsaurus was about 1 meter long and weighed 6 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Chaoyangsaurus at 1 m and the weight at 6 kg.

facts.statement: The skull of Chaoyangsaurus is fourteen centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull is fourteen centimetres long.

facts.statement: Five specific anatomical traits of Chaoyangsaurus were identified as unique autapomorphies distinguishing it from other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The last five traits were considered autapomorphies.

facts.statement: Chaoyangsaurus was a small dinosaur with light legs, a very short and undeveloped bony frill, a small beak, no horns, and a slender body.
facts.quote: Chaoyangsaurus fue un dinosaurio pequeño, con piernas y patas ligeras, volante óseo muy corto y aún no desarrollado, pico pequeño, sin de cuernos y cuerpo grácil y delgado.

facts.statement: Chaoyangsaurus was a herbivore that ate dominant plants of the era such as ferns, cycads, and conifers.
facts.quote: Chaoyangsaurus, como todos los ceratópsidos, era herbívoro, por lo que se alimentaba de las plantas predominantes de la era, como helechos, cicádeas y coníferas.

facts.statement: Chaoyangsaurus lived before Protoceratops and Psittacosaurus, which are considered some of the earliest members of the Ceratopsia family.
facts.quote: Chaoyangsaurus vivió antes que Protoceratops y Psittacosaurus, que se consideran algunos de los primeros miembros de la familia Ceratopsia.

facts.statement: Chaoyangsaurus has been classified in various groups over time, including Chaoyoungosauroidea, Psittacosauridae, and finally confirmed in Chaoyangosauridae.
facts.quote: Fue asignado a Chaoyoungosauroidea por Zhao en 1983, a Psittacosauridae por Zhao en 1985, y a Chaoyangosauridae por Dong en 1992. y confirmado por Zhao et al. en 2006, Han et al. y Zheng et al. en 2015,

facts.statement: It is debated whether Chaoyangsaurus falls outside or inside the Neoceratopia clade.
facts.quote: There were doubts whether it was outside or inside the Neoceratopia.

facts.statement: In 2006, Zhao and colleagues defined Chaoyangsauridae as the most basal clade within the Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: In 2006, Zhao, et al defined a Chaoyangsauridae, as the most basal ceratopian clade.

facts.statement: Due to the scarcity of bones found, the exact length, height, and weight of Chaoyangsaurus remain unknown.
facts.quote: Debido a que se han encontrados escasos huesos de este dinosaurio, se desconoce su longitud, altura y peso.

rejected.statement: The official name Chaoyangsaurus youngi was established in 1999 by Cheng, Zhao, and Xu, giving it priority over previous invalid spellings.
rejected.quote: Cheng, Zhao, and Xu Xing published an official description using the name Chaoyangsaurus youngi, and as the first name for this genus that is not a nomen nudum, it has official priority over all other spellings that have been used.
